articles.headline: Verstappen claims dominant first Singapore GP win
keyFacts: Red Bull driver Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time in his Formula 1 career.
Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton apologized for a strategic error that caused him to finish in sixth place.
Kimi Antonelli finished third and can secure the world championship at the next race in Austin.
body: Singapore GP: Max Verstappen wins event for first time in F1 career ahead of Charles Leclerc as Lewis Hamilton apologises for strategy

Red Bull's Max Verstappen dominated the Singapore Grand Prix with a lights-to-flag victory; Charles Leclerc was second and Kimi Antonelli third; Lewis Hamilton apologised for a messy race strategically that saw him finish down in sixth
Sunday 11 October 2026 15:42, UK

Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time in his Formula 1 career with a dominant victory, while Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton endured a messy race strategically to tumble off the podium late on.

Verstappen led every lap on his way to a second consecutive win despite being unable to communicate with the team due to a radio problem, but it did not affect him as he held off an early challenge from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc who eventually finished seven seconds behind in second.

Kimi Antonelli took advantage of an elbows-out battle late on between Hamilton and McLaren's Lando Norris, with the seven-time world champion on old tyres in the latter stages, to take third and extend his lead over George Russell to 102 points in the Drivers' Championship.

It means Antonelli can become world champion at the next race in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1, should he outscore Russell by 23 points.
Russell recovered to ninth in Sunday's race after starting 19th due to grid penalties for a new power unit, as overtaking proved very difficult at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.
Reigning world champion Norris was fourth ahead of McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri, who also overtook an ailing Hamilton late on.
Hamilton apologised to the team for his strategy, suggesting he made some of the decisive calls that led him to fall down the order on old tyres.
Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson had another strong result in seventh with Audi's Nico Hulkenberg in eighth, while Red Bull's Isack Hadjar went from the pit lane to the points in 10th.
Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto, Alpine's Franco Colapinto, Aston Martin's Lance Stroll and Williams' Alex Albon all retired with reliability issues but no full Safety Cars were required.
Verstappen dominates as Hamilton strategy goes wrong
Coming into the race, pole-sitter Verstappen was concerned about the start as Red Bull have been among the worst starters on the grid throughout 2026.

Leclerc in second had a better initial getaway to almost draw fully alongside Verstappen into Turn 1, but the Dutchman smartly pinched the Ferrari driver and had a better angle to swoop around the outside and, crucially, keep first place.

It looked like Ferrari had more pace early on as Leclerc consistently stayed within one second of Verstappen during the opening 15 laps. However, Verstappen was managing his tyres and began to stretch his lead as the first stint went on, ending up nine seconds ahead by the time Leclerc pitted on lap 25.

The advantage Verstappen built meant he could pit on lap 33 and still emerge in the lead. A Virtual Safety Car for Stroll coming to a halt saw Leclerc pit for fresh softs on lap 39 but he was unable to reel in his 17-second deficit to Verstappen, who won on his 250th grand prix start.
"The last few races have been really positive for us. It's just great to see and we have a lot of motivation in the team to deliver even more results," said Verstappen.
"It's a really good group of people, I really enjoy working with them, and hopefully we can have a bit more fun to the end of the year."
The main story of the Singapore Grand Prix saw a bold strategy by Hamilton go completely wrong, which the British driver held his hand up for post-race.

Starting on mediums, which seemed to be a worse race tyre compared to the softs, Hamilton, in third, was the first of the front-runners to pit on lap 19 so he could get onto the softs as early as possible.
He set some impressive lap times on fresh rubber but was stuck behind Leclerc after the Monegasque driver made his pit stop onto the mediums.
Hamilton felt he was getting held up and when the Virtual Safety Car came out for Stroll's stoppage, Ferrari called him to pit and double stack behind Leclerc, but Hamilton decided to stay out.
"Sorry boys. I let you down today with that strategy. My call, and I lost us valuable points. I'll try and make up for it in the next one," said Hamilton on the radio after the chequered flag.
This left him vulnerable for the remainder of the race on ageing soft tyres as Leclerc quickly caught and overtook him, but that was the least of his problems.

Norris and Antonelli were also catching at a rate of knots and Hamilton thought he could hold on, given the difficulty of overtaking. He got his elbows out against Norris, cutting the first chicane in their battle for third which enabled Antonelli to take fourth from the McLaren driver, before he also passed Hamilton a lap later.

Eventually Norris got through and so did Piastri, who was forced to pit for a second time due to a slow puncture. Given Ferrari were hoping to challenge Verstappen for victory, Hamilton's sixth will be massively frustrating for the team.

articles.headline: Halo Already Delivered the Perfect Master Chief Origin Story, 25 Years Ago
keyFacts: Leaks indicate that Activision is considering a hard reboot for the next Halo game that would serve as Master Chief’s origin story.
Eric Nylund's 2001 tie-in novel, Halo: The Fall of Reach, previously established Master Chief's childhood abduction, military training, and deep bonds with fellow Spartans.
Articles and previous games demonstrate that Spartans are more compelling when depicted as a close-knit family rather than as solitary supersoldiers.
body: Like many gamers in the early 2000s, I got an Xbox specifically so I could play Halo: Combat Evolved. I became so obsessed with it that I bought everything I could find with “Halo” on the cover, including Eric Nylund’s Halo: The Fall of Reach. I didn’t expect it to completely change how I looked at Master Chief, but it did, chronicling his experience as a child abducted into an experimental military program designed to create supersoldiers. The armored, weathered combat veteran from the game, like the rest of us, was once a kid. But even at only six years old, he was special.

Late last month, Xbox announced that development of the next game set in the Halo universe would be handed off to Activision. Then, earlier this week, a leak shared by Rebs Gaming indicated that Activision is considering a hard reboot that would double as Master Chief’s origin story. But not only does this miss the point of Combat Evolved, which thrust players directly into an already ongoing future war between humanity and a messianic alien empire known as The Covenant, it also threatens to overwrite a legitimately great sci-fi story in the process.
The boy inside the armor

The Fall of Reach begins decades before Combat Evolved, in the year 2517, when Dr. Catherine Halsey identifies John as one of 150 children genetically suited for the SPARTAN-II program. These children are abducted and replaced with short-lived flash clones designed to trick their parents into thinking each child is dead. He's then subjected to years of military training under Chief Petty Officer Franklin Mendez. All of this occurs on the planet Reach which, aside from Earth, is positioned as the next most-prominent human world.

Whereas the game and virtually all of its sequels effectively present Master Chief as the last of his kind, The Fall of Reach surrounds him with dozens of Spartans. John grows up alongside Kelly, the fastest of them; Linda, an almost impossibly precise marksman; Fred, who is nearly as capable a leader as John; and Sam, John’s first and closest friend who’s also described as the strongest of them all. Together, they become a found family and tight-knit squad.

Their earliest training exercises establish what ultimately makes John special. He isn’t the fastest or the strongest Spartan. Instead, he earns the others’ trust and inspires bravery. During one exercise, the children are abandoned in the wilderness and told the last one of them to reach an extraction ship will be left behind. John organizes the group and ensures that nobody is abandoned, even though it means openly defying orders. That kind of loyalty makes the Spartans’ eventual losses sting, since we know almost all of them die when the Covenant destroy Reach shortly before the events presented in the original game.

When the 75 candidates undergo the procedures meant to enhance their strength, speed, senses, and reflexes, 30 die and another 12 are left severely disabled. Only 33 emerge as active Spartans. The procedure turns John into something beyond human, but it also forces him to watch more than half of the only family he knows die or disappear overnight. At this point in the story, he's 14 years old.

In one particularly memorable scene from the book, John is testing out the limits of his new body in the gym. Weights feel too light. Objects move too slowly. When a group of four older soldiers harass him and move to attack, he effortlessly kills two and gravely injures the other two in seconds. When John asks Mendez whether the men were enemies or teammates, his instructor refuses to give him a straight answer, which makes it seem like the whole thing was a staged test. Scenes like this represent the start of John’s legend and explain why, when he marches onto the Pillar of Autumn’s bridge early in Halo, several crewmembers turn and stare with awe. It also communicates how he fits in with the rest of human society outside of being merely looked at as a weapon.

That gets to the heart of what makes Nylund’s novel so interesting: It shows us other people who just know Master Chief as John. They tease him, challenge him, follow him, and occasionally understand what he is thinking without any need for words. These relationships make his stoicism feel less like an absence of personality and more like the emotional armor of someone who has spent his entire life losing people.

Late in the book, John meets Cortana and tests the upgraded MJOLNIR Mark V armor that he wears in Combat Evolved. The supposedly controlled exercise is secretly sabotaged, forcing John and Cortana to dodge live ammunition, mines, and an incoming missile. Other Spartans may be stronger, faster, or more naturally gifted, but Cortana recognizes the elusive quality that Halsey first saw in John when he was six: Luck.
Halo is better when Spartans fight together

That same focus on a full team of Spartans is a major reason Halo: Reach remains one of the best games in the franchise. Rather than sending another solitary supersoldier through the Covenant war, Bungie surrounded the player with Noble Team. Carter, Kat, Jun, Emile, Jorge, and Noble Six all have distinguishable specialties and personalities. Unlike with Master Chief, we also see most of them without their helmets on at different points, which humanizes the character and makes the story feel that much more personal.

Most of Noble Team consists of Spartan-IIIs, members of a later program designed to produce cheaper and more expendable supersoldiers. Jorge-052 is the exception. He is a Spartan-II like Master Chief. Even though Jorge isn’t explicitly mentioned in The Fall of Reach, there are a number of unnamed Spartans we simply never meet in the book.

Halo: Reach is the furthest thing from an adaptation of Nylund’s novel, though it does have some overlapping subject matter. What they share more than anything is an understanding that Spartans are more compelling as a family than as interchangeable armored supersoldiers. Their camaraderie gives their sacrifices meaning.
The Halo origin story that almost didn’t happen

It's remarkable that The Fall of Reach established so much of the franchise considering how quickly it was produced. Nylund reportedly wrote the novel in only seven weeks, working from an approved outline and a story bible for a video game that hadn’t even been released yet.

The book arrived on Oct. 30, 2001 — 16 days before Halo: Combat Evolved. That technically makes this tie-in novel the first released piece of Halo media. Readers could learn John’s history, meet his fellow Spartans, and witness the fall of Reach before anyone had set foot on the titular ringworld.

The novel also reportedly came close to never existing because Bungie was resistant to giving Master Chief a defined backstory. Those concerns are understandable: A mostly silent protagonist made it easier for players to imagine themselves inside the armor. But The Fall of Reach proved John could be both an effective player avatar and an interesting character at the same time.

Nylund later returned to the series for Halo: First Strike and Halo: Ghosts of Onyx, chronicling what happened to Master Chief and some of the other Spartans after the first game and through the end of Halo 2. Together, the three novels form a loose trilogy about the soldiers left outside the games’ spotlight.

The largely maligned game Halo 5: Guardians does reunite Master Chief with Fred, Kelly, and Linda. For readers of Nylund’s novels, seeing Blue Team together in a game is monumental. But for anyone who had only played the mainline series, it’s a plot development that feels half-cooked. That disconnect was one of Halo 5’s fundamental storytelling problems.

A new game about John’s origins has the chance to do something similar. Activision doesn’t need to discard The Fall of Reach or assume that its audience has already read it. It can bring the novel’s best ideas into the games properly: John learning to lead Kelly and Sam as a child, the devastating augmentation process, his first missions with Blue Team, the emergence of the Covenant, and the moment Cortana chooses him not because he is the strongest or fastest Spartan, but because he is the bravest and the luckiest.

If Activision really is developing a Master Chief origin story, The Fall of Reach should be its blueprint. Nylund understood that the most interesting question was never how John-117 became strong enough to save humanity. It was how a kidnapped little boy held on to enough of his humanity to become its greatest hero.

articles.headline: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua set to make history with huge £26 million gate
keyFacts: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will fight in Cardiff on December 11 in a sell-out event.
Dana White said the event is expected to generate a gate of £26 million, marking the biggest in British boxing history.
The fight will not break global gate records, which remain held by bouts including Floyd Mayweather versus Manny Pacquiao.
body: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua is already making British boxing history before a punch has even been thrown.
Fury and Joshua will meet in a blockbuster clash on December 11 in Cardiff, with the heavyweight attraction seen as one of the biggest sporting events in British history.
Fury and Joshua’s event has sold out, with 80,000 tickets snapped up in just minutes for the Battle of Britain Getty
The long-term rivals will finally settle their feud after over a decade in the making, in a fight that is worth close to £150 million to both fighters.
But the hotly anticipated clash is already proving history-defining months out from the fight night.
Close to 80,000 spectators will pack out the Principality Stadium with tickets selling out in around an hour for the captivating duel.
And prices ranged from £80 all the way up to £13,000 for the best seats in the house.
As a result, the event has raked in a gate that will become the biggest in boxing history.
That is according to Zuffa Boxing’s Dana White , whose role in the event is in a personal capacity with Turki Alalshikh rather than as an official promoter.
He has suggested the event will rake in an expected gate of $34 million [£26 million] which will make it the biggest in British boxing history.
White told Sky Sports : “I think there’s less than 700 tickets left. You can consider this thing a sellout already.
“There were over 500,000 people in the [ticket] queue. Incredible. But for our generation, two of the biggest, most famous heavyweights in boxing.
“And not even arguable it’s the biggest UK fight ever between two British heavyweights.
White is stunned by the success of the event, which will come close to the Crawford vs Canelo clash he promoted Getty
“Definitely. It will. I don’t want to mis-speak here but we have this thing scaled for around $34 million [£26 million].”
The event would top the British rankings, with Fury and Joshua involved in the other two fights in the top three.
Joshua and Daniel Dubois ‘ 2024 clash brought in £14 million at Wembley Stadium, while Fury’s win over Dillian Whyte generated £12 million at the same venue.

articles.headline: Double Dutch, the competitive sport giving young athletes strength and support
keyFacts: Khnaue Robinson and her Floyd-Little Double Dutch Team in Newark train for and compete in major championships.
Competitive Double Dutch requires physical strength, endurance, precise timing, and close teamwork between turners and jumpers.
Robinson stated that the sport provided her with a supportive community that built her confidence and resilience.
body: For many people, Double Dutch brings back memories of playground games and childhood fun. However, beyond the simple image of jumping rope is a highly competitive sport that requires speed, strength, teamwork, and dedication. Across the world, athletes train seriously for competitions, transforming a traditional activity into a challenging performance sport. For Khnaue Robinson, Double Dutch has become much more than competition, it has become a source of confidence, friendship, and support.

Khnaue Robinson is a member of the Floyd-Little Double Dutch Team based in Newark, New Jersey. At 17 years old, she has already spent five years developing her skills in the sport. Her team practices multiple times each week and competes throughout the year, working toward major competitions where athletes from different teams compete for championship titles.

The Floyd-Little Double Dutch Team has achieved remarkable success, earning 19 World Championship titles. For members of the team, competition season is a time of intense preparation. Every athlete works toward improving speed, accuracy, and coordination because even small improvements can make a difference during a performance.

Competitive Double Dutch requires far more than simply jumping over ropes. Two rope turners create a moving rhythm while the jumper performs fast footwork, tricks, and athletic movements inside the ropes. Timing and teamwork are essential because every person involved must work together perfectly.

Speed is one of the most important elements in competition. Athletes must jump as quickly as possible while maintaining control and precision. Success requires endurance, physical strength, focus, and a positive mindset. A strong competitor must also learn how to recover from mistakes and continue performing under pressure.

For Khnaue, Double Dutch has provided something even more valuable than athletic achievement. Growing up in Newark, she experienced challenges that made finding a supportive environment especially important. The sport gave her a place where she felt safe, accepted, and surrounded by people who cared about her.

She describes the team as more than a group of athletes. It became a community where she could build relationships and find encouragement. The support she received through Double Dutch helped her understand the importance of having people who believe in her abilities.

In Double Dutch, success is not only measured by trophies. The sport teaches discipline, teamwork, confidence, and resilience. Athletes learn that improvement comes from practice and that setbacks are part of the journey toward becoming stronger.

For young people, activities like Double Dutch can provide positive opportunities to develop skills while building meaningful connections. A team can become a place where athletes discover their abilities and receive the support they need to grow.

Khnaue Robinson's story shows that Double Dutch is far more than a game. It is a competitive sport that challenges athletes physically while creating a powerful sense of community. Through every jump, turn, and competition, it continues to prove that teamwork and encouragement can help people achieve more than they imagined.

articles.headline: Liverpool v Manchester City: Premier League – live
keyFacts: Over 600 Manchester City fans received a police escort to Anfield ahead of their Premier League match against Liverpool.
Manchester City play Liverpool following the club being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.
Both teams face squad challenges, with Liverpool missing key players due to injuries sustained during the international break.
body: A group of over 600 Manchester City fans were given a police escort across Stanley Park, chanting as they went about their owners and throwing abuse back at any Liverpool fans who took issue. The message was a clear one of defiance from the hardcore away support.

Enzo Maresca’s first public display since Manchester City were found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules was controlled – apart from the sole, and telling, slip-up of his very first answer.

In Thursday’s pre-emptive PR move, the club had Maresca tell their channels that he was aware of the “noise” around City. Fast forward 24 hours, and to a packed media conference of 45 attendees – around a threefold increase on the norm – at the Etihad Campus, the Italian was asked if this was dismissive of the anger felt towards the club’s cheating. “I understand the reason why most of you are here but the only thing I can say is that there is a process ongoing and in this moment I completely trust the club,” he replied.

This correspondent’s radar bleeped at the use of “in this moment” and, when the microphone was passed, Maresca was quizzed if this meant he may change his mind. “Sorry, that was the wrong answer. I completely trust the club in this moment, in the future, always.” But there was no denying the initial response and how this points to these shaky times for all at City.

It’s Wednesday afternoon (UK time) and I find myself interviewing Tony Hadley on TalkSport about his upcoming big band tour. We play a bit of Spandau Ballet, chat about the classics and his career – hanging out with Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. In as much as you can deduce in a 10-minute chat on Zoom, Tony seems like an absolute gent.

We do always try to bring it back to sport – Tony is an Arsenal fan, there’s a bit of Arteta, Leeds at the weekend. Tony brings up Billy Bremner and suggests that my co-host Charlie Baker and I are too young to remember him playing. We are, and how wonderful to be called young.

Right at the end I go for a slightly cumbersome question/joke about Manchester City. “And I know Manchester City are top of the league, but they’ll probably be bottom of the league by the end of the season?”

Hadley is a pro. Maybe he’s been waiting for this hardball question about the charges. “You just never know what’s going to happen – the world is a crazy place. I’ve got to add to all the big band songs we’re doing … at the end we do a Christmas catalogue which is great fun as well.” What a sidestep.

Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game.

What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it’s perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales.
Lewis Koumas, 21, makes his full Premier League debut for Liverpool, who are without Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai. Ryan Gravenberch and Victor Munoz also come into the side.
Manchester City make one change from their 5-3 win over Sunderland before the international break: Nico O’Reilly replaces Josko Gvardiol at left-back.
Liverpool (4-2-3-1) Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dirk, Kerkez; Gravenberch, Mac Allister; Munoz, Wirtz, Barcola; Koumas.

A four-match international break has presented a stress test. “The intensity of the squad, the athleticism of it, really, I think it’s designed for the elite,” said the Wales head coach, Craig Bellamy, on the completion of four matches in 11 days. Elite club coaches would disagree. The Nations League and the wider set of international games staged across the globe have been accompanied by a daily list of casualties, club officials viewing matches through their fingers as players pull up and gesture to the bench.

Almost certainly to the disquiet of Enzo Maresca, City’s Elliot Anderson and Marc Guéhi were, alongside Harry Kane, the only England players to start all four Nations League matches, with Nico O’Reilly withdrawing halfway through. Liverpool’s problems appear to run deeper, with Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo, early successes for the Andoni Iraola regime, sustaining injuries with Sweden and the Netherlands respectively. Jérémy Jacquet, another bright spark this season, reportedly strained a hamstring with France.

It was quiet around Anfield three hours before kick-off but there is a sense of what is to come. For £15 you can buy a ‘Guilty’ flag, depicting the City squad in jail or a ‘Cheats’ banner riffing off Oasis’s own style. What larks.

The internet: an apology. It turns out you were right. It was actually a simulation all along. Now, talk to me about chemtrails again. And yes, maybe Vinícius Júnior has been replaced by a handsome, baffled-looking waxwork.

Welcome to the weirdest weekend of them all. We are now post-judgment, post-statement, postlapsarian. As the Premier League prepares to snap back into what must be described, out of habit, as reality, armed with the knowledge its serial champions have been the authors of a 10-year sham supremacy, the first question is fairly simple. How is it going to feel?

There is no precedent for this. Even the state of total confusion feels brittle given City maintain their complete state of innocence and deny all charges. We await the release of Irrefutable Body of Evidence, the great lost Madonna erotic thriller sequel, presumably recast around a steamy three-year regulatory tribunal scenario.
Of all the gin joints in the all the towns in all the world …

Manchester City’s first game after being found guilty of more than a hundred Premier League charges could have been anywhere: the Etihad, the Gtech Stadium, Portman Road, even Priestfield in the Carabao Cup. Instead, the great scriptwriter in the sky has decided it should be at Anfield – home of Liverpool, their biggest modern rivals and the team most affected by City’s success in the last 15 years. The atmosphere is always febrile when City visit Anfield; today, it will be off the charts.

Under normal circumstances, this would be a good time for City to play Liverpool. They have won five out of five in the Premier League, whereas Liverpool are still learning to speak Andoni Iraola’s coaching language and will be without both Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo.

You don’t need a PhD in rocket science to know these are not normal circumstances. To many people, this isn’t so much a football match as a public shaming. City will try to focus exclusively on the football – partly because they believe they have irrefutable proof of their innocence, partly because anyone who wants to finish above Arsenal this season needs every point they can get.

Nobody, not even Biff Tannen, knows what’s going to happen over the next few hours. The only certainty is that there will be banners, banter and bile. In almost 140 years of English league football, there has never been a game like this.

articles.headline: Zelensky to Trump: Ukraine will hold elections if Putin agrees to 60-day ceasefire
keyFacts: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine will organize elections if Russian President Vladimir Putin agrees to a 60-day ceasefire.
President Donald Trump called for a new Ukrainian leader, arguing that Zelensky cannot or will not reach a peace agreement.
Zelensky stated that Ukraine needs a ceasefire to establish the security infrastructure required for people to vote.
body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky responded to President Donald Trump’s calls for new leadership in the war-torn country on Sunday, saying elections will be held if Russian President Vladimir Putin agrees to a two-month ceasefire.
Speaking with ABC News’s This Week , Zelensky said the next leader of Ukraine will be decided by its people and acknowledged the difficulty in holding elections during the war with Russia.

“Please tell Putin: Give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organize elections. Of course, we will be ready for any choice of our people, Ukrainian people,” Zelensky said.
Zelensky said the war poses a challenge to holding elections, as it bars Ukraine from implementing the proper security infrastructure needed for residents to vote for their leader.

“It goes absolutely not secured and it goes out of our law, out of our constitution,” he said. “But the main thing is to have security infrastructure for this to give the possibility of people to vote. Of course, it’s up to Ukrainians when to vote, how to do it, and to choose one or another person.”

Trump called for a new leader in Ukraine on Saturday due to what he described as Zelensky’s inability or reluctance to agree to a peace agreement. The president suggested Ukraine “get a new leader who can make a deal,” signaling a notable rift in Zelensky’s relationship with Washington, which has long provided crucial support for his war against Russia.

Zelensky also addressed Trump’s lashing out at Ukraine for targeting Russian oil refineries, which Trump said has led to high oil prices rather than the U.S. war with Iran, as well as Elon Musk blaming him for the length of the war. Zelensky framed the situation as though pressuring Ukraine were easier than holding Putin accountable.

“These people can’t find a key how to stop Putin,” Zelensky said. “Because it’s more difficult to stop Putin than to pressure others, because it’s more simple to speak about the prices and connect it with Ukraine when everybody in the world understands, because of the war in the Middle East, the prices are rising.”

“They’re increasing because of the war in the Middle East, of the blocking of [the Strait of] Hormuz,” he continued. “Because of these reasons, everybody understands. And if we want to speak with people fairly, if we want to be clear, if we want to speak with our nations openly, we have to stop. I mean, these people have to hear reality. Don’t play games with people.”
TRUMP SAYS UKRAINE NEEDS ‘A NEW LEADER WHO CAN MAKE A DEAL’

Ukraine has launched strikes on Russian oil refineries in recent history, claiming to have disabled 51% of Moscow’s refining capacity. The strikes were bad news for the U.S., as officials are counting on its new diesel agreement with Russia to help bring down fuel prices that have surged due to the two conflicts.
In light of the strikes, Trump accused Zelensky of hitting Russia’s oil refineries to create “problems for the world.”

articles.headline: Russia, Ukraine reach energy cease-fire ‘effective immediately,’ Trump announces
keyFacts: President Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine agreed to an energy cease-fire effective immediately.
The Trump administration blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for driving up United States diesel prices.
Trump announced the United States plans to purchase 300,000 tons of Russian diesel immediately, with additional shipments scheduled later.
body: WASHINGTON — President Trump announced Sunday that Russia and Ukraine have reached an energy cease-fire days after he roiled Kyiv by unveiling a diesel purchasing deal with Moscow.

“Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine,” Trump posted on Truth Social. “Both parties have agreed. Do not break it! Thank you for your attention to this matter.”

Kyiv had been carrying out strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, particularly refineries, in retaliation for similar attacks the Kremlin has carried out in Ukraine. The Trump administration has blamed Ukraine’s attacks on Russian refineries for causing diesel prices to spike.
High diesel prices, which are currently sitting at $6.28 a gallon nationally, according to data from the American Automobile Association, have created midterm headaches for Trump.

Although the US cut off imports from Russia, Energy Secretary Chris Wright has claimed that the Ukrainian attacks against Moscow’s refineries have impacted the global supply of diesel and therefore impacted prices in America.

On Friday, following his call with Russian tyrant Vladimir Putin, Trump announced that the US planned to purchase massive amounts of diesel, including 300,000 tons immediately, 500,000 tons in November, and 1,000,000 tons afterward.
The move drew outrage from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who blasted it as a “betrayal” and sparked bipartisan backlash as well.
Some critics argued that Trump can’t legally purchase diesel from Russia without congressional approval due to the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022.

articles.headline: Ukraine strikes Yandex data centre in third attack on Russian tech giant
keyFacts: A Ukrainian drone strike damaged a Yandex data centre near Moscow in the third attack on the Russian tech company this week.
Kyiv said it targeted Yandex to hit Russian revenue streams and force Moscow to divert resources to repair damage.
Yandex said it suspended operations at the site and is working to restore connectivity to its disrupted services.
body: - Published
Yandex has been forced to pause its operations at a data centre near Moscow after the facility was damaged in a Ukrainian drone strike - the third attack on the Russian tech giant's sites this week.
The company - dubbed "Russia's Google" - said no one was injured at the centre in Vladimir, east of the capital, but some of its services were unavailable to users.
Earlier this week, Yandex said it was struggling to maintain its services after two of its five data centres were hit in Ukrainian strikes.
Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks on infrastructure in recent months as the war between them continues in its fifth year following Russia's full-scale invasion.
Kyiv said it was targeting places that provide revenue streams for Moscow's war machine, and that the attacks could force Russia to divert its resources to repair the damage at Yandex.

Sunday's attack came hours after US President Donald Trump warned that Ukraine should "damn well stop" attacking Russia's oil refineries so Moscow could release more diesel to the global market - a deal that has drawn criticism from Europe and sparked a diplomatic row with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Yandex confirmed on Telegram that its data centre in Vladimir had been damaged and that operations had been "completely suspended", although it said it was working to restore connectivity.

The other strikes against Yandex facilities were on Thursday in Sasovo and Friday in in Kaluga, south-west of Moscow, causing problems for some of its services, such as its AI chatbot and smart home devices.

The tech company - which also runs a food-ordering and taxi app used by tens of millions of people - said at the time that its data centres were critical for the normal operation of its services, and that it was "very difficult to predict" when they would be back online.
Meanwhile, Russian strikes on Ukraine have continued through the weekend.
The State Emergency Service of Ukraine said six people were injured in Russian attacks overnight on four districts in its south-eastern Dnipropetrovsk region.
On Saturday, at least 20 people including four children were killed in Russian attacks on Zaporizhzhia, local officials confirmed.
Russia has previously also struck Ukrainian data centres, causing internet outages and prompting some firms to move their servers abroad.

articles.headline: Oval Office spat to public rebukes: A timeline of Trump-Zelenskyy ties
keyFacts: US President Donald Trump called for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's removal, blaming Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for rising diesel prices.
Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel to lower fuel prices, reversing years of US pressure on Moscow.
Zelenskyy stated Ukraine will continue striking Russian oil refineries until Russia stops attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
body: United States President Donald Trump has called for the removal of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy after blaming the Ukrainian leader for rising diesel prices, which have put pressure on the Republican Party ahead of the November midterm elections.
The criticism on Saturday came as tensions between the US and Ukraine have increased after Trump announced a diesel supply deal with Russia.
“I think it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president,” Trump told reporters at the White House on Saturday, saying Zelenskyy had hurt global diesel supplies with strikes on Russian refineries.
“He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers with diesel fuel because Russia supplies a large portion of the diesel fuel throughout the world,” Trump added.

Zelenskyy on Sunday pushed back, vowing to continue striking Russian oil refineries. “Ukraine will be ready to stop striking Russian oil refineries if Russia stops striking our energy infrastructure,” Zelenskyy wrote on X.
“It is possible to stop strikes on energy infrastructure as early as today, but (Russian President Vladimir) Putin does not want to do so,” he said.

This is not the first time Trump has lambasted Zelenskyy. Their tense relationship goes back to Trump’s first term as president, when he pressured Zelenskyy to investigate his rival, Joe Biden, and his son, Hunter Biden.
Here’s a timeline of some of the occasions when Trump has been critical of Zelenskyy:
October 2026: In his remarks at the White House, Trump criticised Zelenskyy over the lack of a peace deal while demanding an end to Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy facilities.
“I said to him, ‘Do what you want. Don’t hit refineries. There’s plenty of targets. Don’t hit refineries.’ And he went out and he hit,” Trump said. “He better damn well stop.”
“I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal because he could have made many deals, but for some reason, he never does,” Trump added.
Trump, who has been urging Zelenskyy to stop attacking Russian energy infrastructure for weeks, struck a deal with Putin on Friday to buy diesel from Russia in an attempt to reduce high fuel prices.
The deal marked a stunning reversal of years of Washington’s pressure on Russia over its full scale invasion of Ukraine.
Zelenskyy, meanwhile, said every additional $1bn Russia earns from exports would help pay for weapons components, drone upgrades, missile production and the recruitment of mercenaries.
Moscow would only be ready to stop when its ability to fight diminished, he added.

April 2025: On April 15 , Trump criticised Zelenskyy and implied Kyiv had started the war against Russia, saying the Ukrainian leader was “always looking to purchase” US missiles. “You don’t start a war against someone 20 times your size and hope people give you some missiles,” Trump said.

Then on April 23 , he criticised Zelenskyy for making “very harmful” statements after the Ukrainian president pushed back against the idea of ceding occupied Crimea to Russia in a potential peace deal.
Zelenskyy had ruled out ceding any territory, declaring, “There is nothing to talk about – it is our land, the land of the Ukrainian people”.
In a post on his social media platform, Trump accused Zelenskyy of stoking tension by “boasting” that Kyiv would not legally recognise ceding Crimea to Russia.
“This statement is very harmful to the Peace Negotiations with Russia,” Trump said, adding that Russia invaded the Crimean Peninsula and annexed it back in 2014 “without a shot being fired”.

“It’s inflammatory statements like Zelenskyy’s that makes it so difficult to settle this War,” Trump said. “He can have Peace or, he can fight for another three years before losing the whole Country.”
Despite the tension, the two leaders held a private meeting at the Vatican on April 26, 2025, during Pope Francis’s funeral.

Feb 28, 2025: During their fiery Oval Office meeting, Trump and Vice President JD Vance clashed with Zelenskyy over rare earth mineral agreements, security assurances and peace negotiations with Russia.

Trump warned Zelenskyy, “You’re either going to make a deal [on ending the war with Russia] or we’re out,” and accused the Ukrainian leader of having “disrespected” the United States and “overplayed his hand”.
The US president and Vance also berated Zelenskyy for lacking gratitude and refusing to compromise to end the war, with Trump arguing that Zelenskyy was unready for peace.
The meeting devolved into a shouting match and Zelenskyy departed the White House abruptly.

February 19, 2025: A month after returning to power for a second term, Trump called the Ukrainian president a “dictator without elections” and accused him of wanting to keep the “gravy train” of US military support going while Washington tries to end the war with Russia.
In a lengthy and scathing post on his social media platform Truth Social, Trump accused Zelenskyy of taking US money and embroiling the country in an endless conflict.

He later doubled down on those comments, telling an audience at an investment summit in Miami that Zelenskyy had “done a terrible job, his country is shattered, and millions and millions of people have unnecessarily died”.

“A dictator without elections. Zelenskyy better move fast or he’s not going to have a country left. Gotta move. Gotta move fast cause that war’s going in the wrong direction,” Trump said on stage at the Future Investment Initiative (FII) Institute summit.

“In the meantime, we’re successfully negotiating an end to the war with Russia. Something I’ll admit that only Trump is going to be able to do and the Trump administration – we’re going to be able to do it. I think Putin even admitted that,” he said.

“Biden never tried. Europe has failed to bring peace and Zelenskyy probably wants to, maybe he wants to keep the gravy train going. I don’t know what’s the problem, but he has been able. He’s very upset,” he added.
Trump had been critical of Biden’s financial and military support to Ukraine during the war. He had vowed to end the war within 24 hours of his taking office, but later said he was being “sarcastic”.

2024 Campaign trail: On the 2024 US presidential election campaign trail, Trump repeatedly criticised Zelenskyy for not trying hard enough to end Russia’s war on Ukraine. In September, at an election rally speech in North Carolina, Trump lashed out at Zelenskyy for refusing to negotiate, stating that even the “worst deal” or giving up a small amount of territory would be better than ongoing death and destruction.

July 2019: During his first term, Trump repeatedly urged Zelenskyy to work with Rudy Giuliani and the US attorney general to investigate Democratic political rival Joe Biden. That is according to a five-page memo summarising the July 25 call.

At the time of the call, the Trump administration was also withholding from Ukraine nearly $400m in congressionally approved security assistance, prompting speculation the US president was using the money as leverage to get his desired investigations.

Zelenskyy expressed willingness to look into new cases and cooperate with US investigations, though he and Ukrainian officials later maintained they did not feel directly threatened or pressured during the conversation itself.

articles.headline: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine "energy ceasefire" after criticizing Zelenskyy
keyFacts: President Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine agreed to an energy ceasefire.
The announcement followed criticism from President Trump regarding Ukrainian leadership and Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries.
Ukrainian officials previously stated they would stop striking Russian energy infrastructure if Russia stopped its attacks.
body: President Trump said Sunday that Ukraine and Russia have agreed to an "energy ceasefire," shortly after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy vowed to continue striking Russian oil refineries in response to criticism from Mr. Trump.

"Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it! Thank you for your attention to this matter," Mr. Trump wrote in a Truth Social post. It's unclear exactly what the ceasefire entails.

Mr. Trump previously took aim at the Ukrainian president's leadership, suggesting Zelenskyy should be replaced and blaming him for high diesel prices. The Ukrainian president clapped back, saying Russia alone was responsible for .
"Ukraine will be ready to stop striking Russian oil refineries if Russia stops striking our energy infrastructure," Zelenskyy wrote on X.

"It is possible to stop strikes on energy infrastructure as early as today, but (Russian President Vladimir) Putin does not want to do so," he said, adding that any de-escalation must be reciprocal and backed by real guarantees.

The exchange came as Kyiv pressed its campaign against infrastructure deep inside Russia, with a drone attack on Sunday shutting down a data center run by Russian technology giant Yandex, the third strike on the company's facilities in four days. Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4 1/2 years since Moscow's full-scale invasion.
Speaking to ABC News' "This Week" on Sunday morning, Zelenskyy said Ukrainians "want peace."

"About energy, I said it to President Trump ... to his team and to his people several times. We want peace," Zelenskyy said. "We are ready for ceasefire. We are ready to begin from any kind of steps of de-escalation."
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has also pushed back on Mr. Trump's comments, writing on X late Saturday that Zelenskyy was leading the country through a war for its independence.
"He has the support of the Ukrainian people, and they have the right to decide. Statements from abroad only confirm that he is doing his job well," Sybiha wrote.
Mr. Trump it was time for Ukraine to get a new president, suggesting Zelenskyy has not done enough to end the war and blaming him for high diesel prices in the U.S.
"I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal because he could have made many deals and for some reason he never does," Mr. Trump said.

According to an announcement from Mr. Trump on Friday, the U.S. has made a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to buy more than 300,000 tons of diesel from Russia right away, followed by 500,000 tons in November, and 1 million tons after that. Amid the deal, which attempts to address high fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections, Mr. Trump has also urged Zelenskyy for weeks to stop strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy criticized the deal and said it would help fund Russia's war in Ukraine.

Mr. Trump has sought to blame record U.S. diesel prices on Ukraine rather than , which has driven up world energy prices. Ukrainian and European officials reacted to the diesel deal with dismay, saying it will help pay for Russia's war effort.

The Ukrainian drone attack on the Yandex data center in the city of Vladimir, east of Moscow, caused outages across the company's services, leaving users in dozens of Russian cities and in Kazakhstan, Belarus and Armenia unable to order taxis or access banking services, according to Russian independent news outlet Astra.

"As a result of the drone attack, the infrastructure of Yandex's data center in Vladimir was damaged. Operations at the data center have been completely halted. There were no injuries," said the Yandex Cloud Telegram channel, which provides operational updates on service availability.

In Moscow, residents described disruption to everyday tasks. Pavel Belyavskiy, a driver for Yandex Taxi, said it was unclear whether orders were coming through at all, and that on several rides he had to cancel after waiting a long time because he could not reach the passenger.
"I'd press the 'call' button to contact them, but nothing happens," he said. "There's nothing I can do, so I'm just forced to cancel."
Igor Mann said he went to check the status of an order on the Yandex Market shopping platform but the page was unavailable, and connecting through a VPN did not help. "Nothing worked," he said.
Another Moscow resident, Eduard Malyavko, said the outages had "direct impact" and weren't just about "convenience."
"It's also about work," he said, adding that they also affected "healthcare, and everything else."

On Thursday, a drone attack took a Yandex data center offline in the Ryazan region, southeast of Moscow. A day later, Ukrainian drones hit the company's major data center in the Kaluga region, southwest of Moscow, partly putting it out of action, Yandex said.

Yandex, often described as Russia's Google, runs the country's most popular search engine and a wide range of digital services, and is heavily involved in Russia's artificial intelligence development.

articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV to have ‘early-stage’ lung nodule surgically removed
keyFacts: Pope Leo XIV announced he will undergo surgery early this week to remove an early-stage lung nodule discovered during a recent examination.
The Vatican stated the 71-year-old pontiff is scheduled to remain at Rome's Gemelli Hospital for approximately one week while recovering.
The Vatican has not announced any changes to the pope's scheduled trip to South America from November 6 to 17.
body: Pope Leo XIV announced Sunday that he will undergo surgery to remove a nodule discovered in his lung, marking the first major health concern for the 71-year-old pontiff since he became the leader of the Catholic Church last year.

Leo revealed the diagnosis during his weekly Sunday blessing in St. Peter’s Square, telling worshippers that doctors discovered the abnormal growth during a recent examination and recommended its removal.

“It was detected at a very early stage and is well-localized,” Leo said, according to a Vatican translation of his remarks. “The doctors believe that it is best to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it. The operation is already scheduled to take place in the coming days.”
The Vatican said the operation is scheduled for early this week at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital, where the pope is expected to remain for approximately one week while recovering.
The Vatican has not disclosed whether the nodule is cancerous or provided additional details about its size or characteristics.

Lung nodules are small abnormal growths that can be discovered during routine medical imaging. While some are cancerous, many are benign and can result from infections, inflammation, or scar tissue, according to the American Cancer Society.
Leo, the first American-born pope, has no publicly known history of serious health problems and maintains an active lifestyle that includes playing tennis and swimming.

His planned surgery comes less than a month before a scheduled trip to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru from Nov. 6-17. The Vatican has not announced changes to the itinerary, and Leo indicated Sunday that he still intends to travel.
The announcement also comes a day after Leo weighed in on a controversial execution planned in his homeland.

On Saturday, the pope reaffirmed the Catholic Church’s opposition to capital punishment, calling the death penalty “inadmissible” in a social media post marking the World Day Against the Death Penalty.

His remarks followed the Pentagon’s announcement that the Dec. 3 execution by firing squad of Nidal Malik Hasan, who was convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, will be livestreamed . Leo did not address Hasan’s case directly.
REPUBLICAN OPPOSITION GROWS TO LIVESTREAMING EXECUTION OF FORT HOOD SHOOTER
Leo’s upcoming surgery also recalls the health struggles of his predecessor, Pope Francis, who was hospitalized at Gemelli for more than a month in 2025 after developing double pneumonia.
Francis, who had suffered from chronic respiratory problems and had part of his lung removed as a young man, died April 21, 2025, at age 88 , following a stroke.

articles.headline: What to know about the landmark Warner Bros. Discovery sale
keyFacts: Paramount acquired all assets of Warner Bros. Discovery for $111 billion after a bidding war that led Netflix to withdraw from negotiations.

body: Earlier this year, the streaming and entertainment industry witnessed one of its most high-stakes megadeals ever, stunning industry observers. Not only is it historic in its size, but it is also predicted to disrupt Hollywood and the media business as we know it.

After years of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) struggling under the weight of billions of dollars in debt, compounded by declining cable viewership and fierce competition from streaming platforms, the company has been considering major strategic changes, including selling its entertainment assets to one of its rivals.
Several major players saw the potential in acquiring the media giant, and in December, Netflix announced it would acquire WBD’s studios and streaming for $82.7 billion.

But in a surprise eleventh-hour move in late February, the David Ellison-run Paramount became the winner of this bidding war, offering $111 billion to acquire all of WBD’s assets, including its studios, HBO, streaming platforms, games, and TV networks such as CNN and HGTV. Paramount was recently acquired by Ellison with significant support from his father, Larry Ellison — the Oracle chairman, world’s sixth-richest person, and major Trump donor.

Paramount’s offer was approved by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) in June. A federal judge then paused the deal after a lawsuit was filed on July 13 by a coalition of 12 state attorneys general. However, a judge approved it in late September, with the acquisition finally official as of October 6.
Let’s break down exactly what happened and what could come next.
What has happened so far?
This all started back in October 2025 when Warner Bros. Discovery revealed it was exploring a potential sale after receiving unsolicited interest from several major players in the industry.
The bidding process quickly became competitive, and Paramount and Comcast emerged as serious contenders, with Paramount initially viewed as the frontrunner.

However, WBD’s board eventually determined that an offer from the streaming giant Netflix was the most attractive. Netflix offered $82.7 billion for just Warner’s film, television, and streaming assets.

Thus began the bidding war. Paramount believed its bid of approximately $108 billion for all of Warner’s assets was superior to Netflix’s offer that focused on just the studios and streaming. To sweeten its deal, Netflix amended its agreement in January to an all-cash offer at $27.75 per share of Warner Bros. Discovery, further reassuring investors and paving the way for the deal to proceed.

Paramount persisted in its attempts to acquire WBD. Still, the Warner board repeatedly rejected its offers, citing concerns about Paramount’s heavy debt load and the increased risk associated with its proposal, including concern over the suite of investors bankrolling Paramount’s bid, which includes Saudi, Qatari, and Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth funds. The board noted that Paramount’s offer would have left the combined company burdened with $87 billion in debt, a risk they were unwilling to take at the time.

In January, Paramount filed a lawsuit seeking more information about the Netflix deal. A month later, the company sought to sweeten its deal by announcing it would offer a $0.25 per share “ticking fee” to WBD shareholders for each quarter the deal fails to close by December 31, 2026. It also said it would pay the $2.8 billion breakup fee if Warner backs out of its deal with Netflix.

Then, in a final attempt to secure a deal, Paramount increased its offer to $31 per share in February. This prompted the WBD board to prolong discussions with Paramount regarding a potential agreement, considering it as a superior offer. Netflix declined to increase its bid and withdrew from the negotiations.

“The transaction we negotiated would have created shareholder value with a clear path to regulatory approval,” Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters said in a statement on February 26. “However, we’ve always been disciplined, and at the price required to match Paramount Skydance’s latest offer, the deal is no longer financially attractive, so we are declining to match the Paramount Skydance bid.”

In addition to the billions Paramount already holds in debt, the company is also set to assume the approximately $33 billion in debt Warner Bros. Discovery holds under the agreement. The deal will be backed by a $54 billion debt commitment from Bank of America, Merrill Lynch, Citi, and Apollo Global Management, as well as $45.7 billion in equity from Larry Ellison.
Regulatory hurdles and other concerns
In addition to the assumption of substantial debt posing a significant financial burden, Paramount faced several other hurdles in its deal with WBD.

For one, Ellison has warned about significant job reductions that are expected in the near future. There have already been widespread concerns among critics about potential job losses and lower wages.

Ellison is also a controversial figure in the industry, and his ownership of CBS News has been seen as sympathetic and supportive of the administration of Donald Trump, of whom his father, Larry Ellison, is a major donor. Under Ellison’s ownership of Paramount, reporting critical of the administration has been shelved or received increased scrutiny from Ellison or his appointed head of CBS News, the conservative provocateur Bari Weiss.

This has led to some concern among employees at Warner-owned CNN. Trump has personally sought concessions from news divisions critical of him, including a $16 million settlement from CBS, before his FCC would approve the Ellison takeover of Paramount. Before Netflix bowed out of the deal, Trump pressured the company to fire the former Biden White House official Susan Rice from its board. He has publicly stated his intentions to bring CNN to heel under new owners.
Regulatory scrutiny was another hurdle. Such a large-scale merger attracted attention from lawmakers.

For instance, California attorney general Rob Bonta said in a statement on February 26 that “these two Hollywood titans have not cleared regulatory scrutiny — the California Department of Justice has an open investigation, and we intend to be vigorous in our review.”

A day before Netflix backed out, a coalition of 11 state attorneys general urged the U.S. Department of Justice to review the merger under concerns it will stifle competition and increase subscription prices. This comes months after U.S. senators Elizabeth Warren, Bernie Sanders, and Richard Blumenthal voiced their concerns to the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division, warning that such a massive merger could have serious consequences for consumers and the industry at large. The senators argue that the merger could give the new media giant excessive market power, enabling it to raise prices for consumers and stifle competition.

Despite the DOJ approving the deal in June, a coalition of 12 state attorneys general filed a lawsuit on July 13 to block the merger. The suit argues it would lessen competition and harm movie theaters, cable distributors, and viewers. The coalition is led by Bonta, with Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, and Washington also joining.
In response, U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín issued a 14-day pause.
What now?
As of October 6, Paramount and Warner Bros. has officially been renamed Skydance, and the new combined corporation will have annual revenue of almost $70 billion.
In terms of its streaming services— Paramount+, HBO Max, and Discovery+,— those are all set to be combined eventually.

articles.headline: Why it's important to backup data saved on your older thumb drives
keyFacts: Users should backup data stored on older USB thumb drives because the devices face risks of physical loss, hardware failure, and data corruption over time.
Flash storage has a limited number of write cycles and can suffer from bit rot, where cells lose electrical charge and corrupt data.
The 3-2-1 backup rule suggests saving important data in at least three locations, including two local drives and one cloud upload.
body: Why it's important to backup data saved on your older thumb drives
Damage, loss and corruption are all factors worth considering.

Perhaps it's just anecdotal, but USB thumb drives don't seem as popular as they used to be. That would make sense, since they've been rendered unimportant or obsolete for many of the tasks they were built for. Technologies like email, chat and AirDrop make transferring small files a breeze. Larger files are often better stashed and shared using online services like iCloud, or else full-size external SSDs.

You may well be keeping some files on thumb drives, whether because they make sense for your lifestyle, or you're just clinging to media from a decade or two ago. And why wouldn't you? There's nothing more portable than a tiny USB stick. There's also no sense buying extra storage if you don't have to, certainly not with memory prices shooting into the stratosphere.

If you haven't already, though, it's time to create backups for those old thumbies. Their time is running out, either because of the odds of a disaster or the inevitable consequences of their design. You should even consider migrating away from them entirely.
You can't beat the laws of physics

Anything as small as a thumb drive is at high risk of destruction or going missing. You might leave one at the office, or accidentally catapult it out of your bag as you race to catch a plane. And if you move frequently enough, some possessions can seemingly vanish into the ether.

Even without those concerns, there's a ticking clock. All flash storage has a finite number of write cycles, usually somewhere in between 10,000 and 100,000 for a thumb stick. This isn't much of a problem if you only use a drive for archival storage. If you're copying files daily or weekly, however, you're gradually reducing the amount of usable space, until one day the drive won't work at all. With thumb drives, you can't even run TRIM commands to recover some of that room, as you can on regular SSDs.

Adding to this is a less consistent threat known as bit rot. To represent data, flash memory depends on cells holding an electrical charge. Over time, those cells will lose electrons, which may eventually result in flipped bits. That translates into data corruption. Bits can even be flipped by cosmic rays, although the odds are relatively low — about one per gigabyte per month, at least at sea level. Bit rot is likely the least of your worries, yet on a long enough timeline, rare events become a certainty.

It's also worth remembering that while thumb drives don't have any moving parts, they still rely on components like connectors and controller chips. These can fail for various reasons, such as impacts, corrosion or shoddy manufacturing. A drive stored in an especially humid environment could be contaminated with mold.
How should you backup old thumb drives?

If data is truly important, the common rule of thumb (no pun intended) is known as 3-2-1. That is, data should be saved to at least three places: two local drives and one cloud upload. Some people go a step further, making sure one of those drives is at a separate address or in a fireproof safe. That's probably overkill for the average person, yet fires, floods and other disasters do happen.

In any event, you don't want to be entirely dependent on the cloud. On top of subscription fees, internet connections go down, and even billion-dollar datacenters can suffer catastrophic failures. You also don't want your data at risk if a business turns unethical. Some businesses play loose with security, or don't see any problem collaborating with authoritarian governments.

When files are less than critical but still nice to have, just make sure your copies are somewhere easily identifiable and retrievable. Your computer's internal drive(s) might do, although you're still better off with the cloud or an external SSD. If a computer stops working, retrieving files from it may be complicated, requiring you to physically extract a drive and find some means of plugging it into another machine.

articles.headline: This Control-inspired action game set in a 'planet-scale alien mind' has one of the most stunning art styles I've seen this year
keyFacts: Studio Lifeforms announced Etre, an upcoming narrative-driven action adventure game set on a sentient alien world called Orbis.
Studio Lifeforms stated that the game features visuals inspired by 1970s and 1980s graphic novels and a combat system influenced by Remedy's Control.
Studio Lifeforms has not yet announced an official release date for the game.
body: In the age of near photorealism, it takes a lot for a game's visuals to impress me. As cramming yet more pixels into a videogame character's face provides diminishing returns, standing out from the crowd is increasingly about how creative developers get in applying that power. All that said, I was genuinely mesmerised by the debut footage of Etre, an upcoming action adventure game with a truly eye-popping art style.

Created by LA-based developer Studio Lifeforms, Etre is a narrative driven-action game set on Orbis, which Studio Lifeforms describes as a "planet-scale alien mind on the brink of awakening". You play as a character named Xyle, who arrives at this sentient cityscape in search of his soulmate Atel.

According to Studio Lifeforms, the game's distinctive visuals are inspired by graphic novels of the '70s and '80s. Studio Lifeforms doesn't specify which graphics novels, and I am too much of a comics philistine to tell you. But the result is an incredibly distinctive visual style. In terms of games, Etre's closest visual cousins are the likes of Rez and Tetris Effect. But Etre applies its aesthetics to a much more grounded type of game.

From a mechanical perspective, Studio Lifeforms cites Remedy's Control as the primary influence, with the game letting you explore Orbis in a semi-open fashion, while the story will be shaped by your actions on Orbis. Like Control, Etre features a highly movement-based combat system. Also like Control, the enemies you fight are super weird, including environmental anomalies and "living geometry."

While I'm transfixed by Etre's art, I will say that, in the few clips present on the Steam page, the combat looks a little flat. One of the great things about Control was how it fully delivered on both a weird setting and the joy of obliterating enemies by cobbing massive chunks of concrete at then. Pretty as it is, Etre can't rely on good looks alone, and will need that tactile satisfaction to back it up.
For now, though, Etre being pleasing to look at is enough. Studio Lifeforms hasn't announced a release date yet, but I'd expect Etre to arrive sometime next year.

articles.headline: Minnesota GOP chair blasts progressive group over KKK-themed sign shown during Black House speaker's remarks
keyFacts: Progressive group Sunrise Movement Twin Cities disrupted a Minnesota Republican dinner, holding a KKK-themed sign while House Speaker Lisa Demuth spoke.
GOP Chair Alex Plechash accused demonstrators of racial intimidation, while the group said they protested policies harming marginalized communities.
Eagan police issued trespass orders after the event, and potential charges remain under investigation, according to Plechash.
body: Minnesota's Republican Party chairman is accusing protesters of racial intimidation after demonstrators disrupted a GOP dinner and displayed a sign invoking the Ku Klux Klan while the state's first Black female House speaker addressed the crowd.

Minnesota GOP Chair Alex Plechash blasted the demonstrators in a statement after Friday night's Lincoln Reagan Dinner in Eagan, where protesters held a sign reading "RepubliKKKan Party" during remarks by House Speaker and Republican gubernatorial candidate Lisa Demuth .

"Last night, radical protesters stormed the stage at our Lincoln Reagan Dinner and held up a KKK symbol while Speaker Lisa Demuth spoke," Plechash said in a statement posted to X by the Republican Party of Minnesota.
DAVID MARCUS: MINNESOTA GOP CANDIDATES KEEP TRUMP AT ARM'S LENGTH AS THEY EYE A POST-TRUMP PARTY FUTURE
"Let's be clear about what happened. Left leaning protesters aimed a symbol of racial terror at a Black woman leader, at a dinner named for the president who ended slavery," he continued.

Sunrise Movement Twin Cities, a progressive activist organization, claimed responsibility for the disruption and said the demonstration was intended to protest Republican policies it believes harm immigrants and marginalized communities, according to local news station KTSP .
"We disrupted this fundraiser because we refuse to give a moment's peace to the people bankrolling racial violence," the group said in a statement cited by the outlet.
The organization also said it was not affiliated with Minnesota's Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party (DFL).
Video of the incident shows demonstrators moving toward the front of the room holding signs, including one with the letters "KKK" highlighted in red, according to outlet.
One protester could be heard shouting, "You love Trump and you will not stand up for Minnesotans," as Demuth stood on stage holding a microphone.
As security escorted the demonstrators away, attendees began chanting, "Lisa," followed by chants of, "USA."
Plechash told the outlet that protesters gained access to the dinner by purchasing tickets and passing through security checkpoints.
KLOBUCHAR'S FRAUD FIGHT CLAIM TAKES HIT AFTER GOP OPPONENT COMBS THROUGH RECEIPTS: 'WHERE WERE YOU?'
The chairman said the event experienced two disruptions, the first during remarks by Republican U.S. Senate candidate Michele Tafoya and the second while Demuth was speaking.

Plechash said roughly three or four protesters pushed toward the front of the room carrying banners during Demuth's remarks. He estimated the disruption lasted about 30 seconds and said he did not believe the demonstrators posed a physical threat.
Plechash said in his X post that Eagan police issued trespass orders and that potential charges remained under investigation.
The GOP chairman also called out Minnesota Democrats, specifically naming the Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party, Sen. Amy Klobuchar and Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan.
"Intimidation, criminal behavior, and racist rhetoric have no place in Minnesota politics," Plechash wrote.
"Republicans debate ideas, and we'd welcome the DFL to show up and do the same," he added. "Every hour they stay silent says something. Their silence is deafening."
Demuth, who won Minnesota's Republican gubernatorial primary in August, will face off against Klobuchar, the Democratic nominee, in November's election to succeed Gov. Tim Walz .

Ten-man Southampton secured their first South Coast derby win in the league in over two decades with a 1-0 home victory over Portsmouth.

Portsmouth looked the more industrious team at the start of only the 35th league meeting in history between these sides - but it was Southampton who broke the deadlock.

Finn Azaz's magnificent ball found Bree, who had easily slipped from the grasp of Jayden Meghoma. He took one sharp touch to control it and another to guide it beyond Nico Schmid, before celebrating in the direction of the Pompey fans.

Few chances of note followed before the break, but the hosts suffered a huge blow moments before the whistle. Boyhood Saints fan Bragg picked up a second booking for a needless pull on Ebou Adams and walked.

John Mousinho brought on Adrian Segecic at the break to try and help find the equaliser, then made a triple change just after the hour - but he was unable to refresh the visitors' attack, which increasingly lacked urgency.
That was illustrated in the numbers: 10 second-half shots, zero on target, 0.51 xG.

A run of four straight draws in this fixture comes to an end - capping a positive week for Southampton, following the news Tonda Eckert was given only a six-week suspended ban by the FA for the 'Spygate' saga.
Eckert: Derby win means everything - but we had to dig deep after red
Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert speaking on Sky Sports:
"It means everything. We had to dig deep, probably a lot deeper than we thought before the game and credit to the boys because they deserved that."
On the red card: "You know how much it means to him [Bragg].

"At the end, I said to him he gave us a game we would not have had any other way, so we'll probably look back at the end of the season and say this is the game that gave us a big push and he was a part of that. In a different way than he wanted, but it happens. It will be a learning for him.
"I think it did change the game. Not on the scoreline, but the game changes then and you need to find different qualities. We knew then we had to dig deep."
Mousinho bemoans Pompey's inability to take advantage of extra man
Portsmouth head coach John Mousinho speaking on Sky Sports:

"When you come away from games and you're well beaten, it's easier to take in some ways. Today, it was a different game after the red card, but for the amount of pressure we had in the second half, the amount of opportunities we had, to not put the ball in the back of the net... we're devastated.

"There's very few times you come in as a head coach or manager after the game and not be frustrated by the way you've conceded goals. We lost a challenge in the middle of the park, had half-decent movement in behind, but it's something we highlighted. We have to be much better and we actually got away with one after the first or second minute.

"Against a really good side, if you get torn apart - and they had some spells in the first half where they looked good, but didn't really threaten us - you hold your hands up and take it. But it's one we'll look back on.
"For the territory and the opportunities we created, it was a good performance against 10 men - we just didn't put the ball in the back of the net."

articles.headline: Trump urges John Fetterman to switch parties: ‘I’d love to see him as a Republican’
keyFacts: Donald Trump encouraged Democratic US Senator John Fetterman to switch to the Republican party ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.
Fetterman has repeatedly rejected joining the Republicans, stating he votes overwhelmingly with Democrats despite recent policy splits with his party.
If Democrats win four seats to retake the Senate majority, Fetterman could gain influence, reducing his incentive to switch parties.
body: Donald Trump on Saturday openly encouraged Democratic US senator John Fetterman to switch parties and become a Republican just weeks before the federal midterm elections could reshape control of Congress.

“I’d love to see him as a Republican,” the presidents told reporters at Joint Base Andrews as he returned to Washington DC from a rally in Tennessee. “He does better as a Republican than he does as a Democrat.”

The comments were among the most direct overtures by Trump to woo Fetterman into his Republican party, a matter of growing importance as the GOP could lose its Senate majority in November’s midterms. With his everyman appeal, Fetterman was a Democratic star when he was first elected to the Senate in 2022. But during his time in Washington, he has split with Democrats on issues ranging from immigration to Israel, leading to speculation that he might switch parties.
A representative for Fetterman did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Fetterman has repeatedly rejected the notion of becoming a Republican, writing in the Washington Post in May that he would be a “terrible Republican who still votes overwhelmingly with Democrats”. His relationship with fellow Democrats became more tenuous after he recorded a video for the Republican midterm convention in September praising his fellow Pennsylvania senator, Republican Dave McCormick, suggesting there were extremists in his party.
“I’m always going to stand with America,” Fetterman said in the video. “I’m always going to reject the extremes and socialism and that anti-American way of life.”
Also in September, Fetterman described himself seemingly inadvertently as a “lifelong Republican” during a fireside chat at the Texas Tribune festival in Austin.

Such flirtations with the Republican party – if not his slip of the tongue in Austin – could make it extremely difficult for Fetterman to win the Democratic nomination for another term in the Senate. Trump raised that prospect on Saturday as he encouraged the party switch.

Democrats need to pick up four seats to retake the Senate majority, a once remote prospect that remains challenging for the party. But Trump’s unpopularity and the economic fallout from the Iran war have intensified headwinds for the Republican party, making Democrats more bullish about a path to Senate control.
If Democrats picked up the four seats for a 51-seat majority, that could put Fetterman in an influential position, reducing the incentive to switch parties.

The last senator whose party switch affected control of the chamber was Jim Jeffords of Vermont, who left the GOP in 2001 to give Democrats a narrow majority. Former Pennsylvania US senator Arlen Specter’s decision to abandon Republicans in 2009 helped Democrats achieve a supermajority.
- Guardian staff contributed reporting
